title: KV Cache Autopilot: Safety Envelope, Shadow Replay, and Staged TTL Annealing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated recommendation and safe-apply system (Autopilot) for KV/prefix caching that proposes batching-aware cache keys, TTL schedules, and policy envelopes. The system will use shadow-replay simulation and confidence bands to avoid regressions to latency, throughput, or cost, and provide a deterministic staged-apply + rollback playbook for operators.
background: Current manual tuning of prefix TTLs and cache keys is time-consuming and error-prone. Previous TTL playbooks improved hit-rate but still required heavy guardrails. We need a component that generates recommendations from production traffic traces, quantifies risk via counterfactual shadow replays, and applies changes with safety envelopes (rate limits, impact thresholds, automatic rollback).
objectives: Automate generation of cache-key proposals and per-prefix TTL schedules informed by batching behavior
Quantify hit-rate and downstream token-cost impact with shadow-replay simulations
Provide safe staged-apply with canary + gradual annealing and automatic rollback on predefined SLO regressions
Expose explainability for recommended changes so SREs/PMs can review before apply
success_metrics: 10-25% reduction in per-token serving cost for targeted workloads (measured in cost/token)
No more than 1.0% increase in 95th percentile generation latency during canary windows
>90% of automated changes pass shadow replay confidence threshold without manual intervention
Mean time to rollback < 5 minutes when automated rollback triggers
approach: Trace sampling: collect representative prefix+batching contexts using low-overhead sampler (1-2% traffic) with request attribution metadata
Hit-modeling: build prefix-level hit probability curves conditioned on request batch size and sequence-length distribution
Cost simulation: shadow-replay traces through candidate policy (new keys/TTLs) to estimate token-level cost delta and latency impact
Safety envelope: compute per-prefix confidence bands and global impact budget; only recommend changes that fall within envelope
Staged apply: apply to small canary cohort, observe live metrics with short rolling windows, and progressively widen if safe
Rollback automation: define detectors and an automated rollback runner that can revert changes within SLA windows
experiments: Offline shadow-replay run on 14 days of sampled traffic to evaluate hit-rate uplift across candidate key schemes
A/B canary applying TTL annealing to 1% of traffic with circuit-breaker thresholds on latency/cost/serving errors
Batch-awareness ablation: evaluate recommendation quality with and without batch-conditioned hit models
simulation_results: Initial offline shadow replay (Feb 2026) on e-commerce and messaging workloads showed median hit-rate uplift of 8% with a projected 12% token-cost decline when combining prefix rekeying and TTL staggering. 95th-latency simulated worst-case increased by 0.9% for one workload and 0.2% for another. Confidence intervals computed with bootstrap resampling were tight enough for a subset (~60%) of prefixes.
rollout_plan: 1) Run full shadow-replay analysis and generate ranked recommendations (non-destructive) for owners
2) Review UI: show explainability, delta in cost and latency, and confidence band per recommendation
3) Canary apply to single region and 0.5% user cohort for 2 hours with telemetry hooks
4) If canary stable, anneal TTLs on 10% cohort over 24 hours, then 50%, then 100%
5) Automate rollback if any detector breach occurs (see rollback_playbook)
rollback_playbook: Detectors: 95p latency + error rate + token-cost over baseline; threshold: relative change > 2x confidence band or absolute 1.0% latency increase
Immediate automated rollback: revert policy and force KV metadata refresh if detector trips during canary
Mitigation steps: if rollback fails, trigger traffic routing to fallback model variant and escalate to oncall
Postmortem: require a blameless review and update recommendation filters before reattempt
acceptance_criteria: Autopilot can generate ranked recommendations with explainability UI for >90% of high-volume prefixes
Shadow-replay simulator completes a 7-day sample in < 3 hours for 100M requests baseline on staging cluster
Safe apply flow can perform a canary apply and subsequent automated rollback when detectors breach
Documentation and runbooks are published and reviewed by SRE and Platform PM
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shadow replay diverges from live behavior due to non-deterministic side effects. Mitigation: prioritize low-side-effect traces and add a conservative live validation stage.
Risk: Overfitting recommendations to sampled data. Mitigation: use cross-day validation and require recommendations to pass multiple sample windows.
Risk: Policy churn causes thrash on KV metadata. Mitigation: rate-limit applies and enforce cool-down periods per-prefix.
Risk: Automated rollback flaps. Mitigation: use backoff on retry and human-in-loop for repeated rollbacks.
notes: This ticket focuses on the model and orchestration layers for recommendations. UI polish and RBAC gating will be separate PM tickets. We should coordinate with the Console team for explainability panels and with Security for any KMS interactions if metadata includes sensitive identifiers.
